# Help from Anywhere

**You don't have to be in the room to help build this.**

Conductor is a free, private tool that lets a group of people coordinate in real time using nothing but their phones — everyone's phone plays the same timed cues at the same moment, so a crowd can freeze, wave, light up, or move together on a shared beat. No app store, no accounts, no server. If you've never seen it, open the demo first: <https://quidam2k.github.io/conductor/index.html?demo>

We record voice cues and write event scripts together in person every couple of weeks. But a lot of the most useful work doesn't need a meeting — you can do it on your own time, from anywhere, and send it in. This page is that work.

*Generated September 2, 2026 · week of September 1, 2026. This page updates on a regular cadence — check back for the current ask.*

## What we could use this week

Pick **one** of these. Any single one genuinely helps — you don't need to do all three.

- **Record a short voice pack for one demo event** — Pick any bundled demo (The Stillness is the shortest — about six cues). Record every cue in your own voice with the in-app recorder and export it as a pack .zip. Clear, calm, one to three seconds each.
- **Write one new short event script** — Four to eight cues, plain text, something a small crowd could pull off in a public space (a freeze, a wave, lights up, a slow turn). No recording needed — the script alone is genuinely useful.
- **Try to break it and tell us how** — Open the app cold on your own phone, run the demo with the screen locked in your pocket, and note anything confusing, silent, or wrong. A plain-language bug report is worth as much as a recording.

---

## How to record voice cues (step by step)

You record right inside the app — no separate software, no account. Do it on the phone or laptop you already have.

1. Open the app: <https://quidam2k.github.io/conductor/> — check the bottom of the screen says **v62** or higher.
2. Load an event to record for. Easiest: tap **Try the Demo** to load "The Stillness," or tap **Create New Event** and write a short script (4–8 cues).
3. Go into the editor for that event. Next to each action you'll see a **🎤 Record** button.
4. Tap **🎤 Record** on an action, say the cue clearly (a second or two — "freeze", "hold", "get ready"), and stop. Tap **✓ Use & Next** to keep it and move on.
5. When you've recorded every cue, go to the **Review & Share** step and **export the recordings as a resource pack** — that gives you a single `.zip` file.
6. Rename the `.zip` to something we'll recognise (like `stillness-yourname.zip`) and send it to us (see below).

**Recording tips:** somewhere quiet, normal speaking pace, keep each cue to one to three seconds, and keep the volume even across cues. It plays through a phone speaker in a noisy crowd, so clear beats fancy.

---

## What to send

- **A resource pack `.zip`** (your recorded voice cues), and/or
- **An event script** — either a `.txt`/`.json` file, or the plain text pasted straight into your message, and/or
- **A bug report** — just describe what you did, what you expected, and what actually happened.

Whatever you've got. A single recorded cue or a two-line bug note is worth sending.

---

## Where to send it

- **Open a GitHub issue and attach your file** *(easiest — works today, no account of ours, nothing to sign up for)*: [open a new issue](https://github.com/Quidam2k/conductor/issues/new). Describe what you're sending, drag your `.zip`/`.txt` into the issue, and submit. A free GitHub account is the only requirement.
- **Discord:** a project chat invite is coming soon — for now, the GitHub issue above is the reliable way in.
- **Not sure where something goes?** Open an issue on [the project on GitHub](https://github.com/Quidam2k/conductor) and ask. No question is too small.

## Coming in person instead?

We meet in person to record together roughly every couple of weeks. Can't make it? Everything on this page is designed so you can help on your own time and send it in — you don't need to be in the room.
